study.title: Acupuncture Treatment Decreased Temporal Variability of Dynamic Functional Connectivity in Chronic Tinnitus
study.study_design: Resting-state fMRI study; chronic tinnitus patients measured before and after acupuncture; compared with age- and sex-matched normal subjects
study.population: 17 chronic tinnitus patients and 22 age- and sex-matched normal subjects
study.inclusion_criteria: (i) between 18 and 70 years of age, right-handed; (ii) subjective neurological tinnitus, patients reported that they heard sound on the unilateral or bilateral tinnitus, no history of acupuncture treatment; (iii) no magnetic resonance contraindications; (iv) no medical history with congenital or hereditary disease, endocrine immune disease, mental or neurological system disease or the severe disease of heart, liver, or kidney, and so on
study.exclusion_criteria: (i) left-handed; (ii) other subjective tinnitus, objective tinnitus (including mechanical or pulsatile tinnitus), or acute tinnitus; (iii) magnetic resonance contraindications; (iv) pregnant, breastfeeding, or menstruating; (v) medical history with congenital or hereditary disease, endocrine immune disease, mental or neurological system disease, or the severe disease of heart, liver, or kidney, and so on; (vi) the history of mental or neurological medicine

arms.dropouts: 6 excluded as acute tinnitus patients; 10 withdrew consent

conditions.source_location: Pages 3, 5, Data Acquirement and Results sections

conditions.timepoint_exact: 2 days after a course of acupuncture treatment

interventions.needle_size_exact: 0.35 mm in diameter and 40 mm in length
interventions.manipulation_exact: the acupuncturist manipulated the needle within the tolerance of the subject until the subjects obtained the deqi sensation without sharp pain
interventions.practitioner_description_exact: specialized and licensed acupuncturists (Jun Yang and Bixiang Zha)
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: all patients were instructed to avoid starting other interventions; patients didn't receive other supplementary medicine, electroacupuncture, or moxibustion throughout the course of acupuncture
interventions.treatment_rationale_exact: Additional acupoints were selected according to meridian diagnosis and the patient's symptoms

sensory_interoceptive_responses.value_exact: the acupuncturist manipulated the needle within the tolerance of the subject until the subjects obtained the deqi sensation without sharp pain
sensory_interoceptive_responses.notes: Deqi is described qualitatively as a target sensation; no formal deqi scale or subscale scores are reported

neuroimaging_methods.sequence_exact: gradient spin echo planar imaging sequence (functional); 3D T1 BRAVO sequence (structural)
neuroimaging_methods.scan_duration_exact: 520.8 s (total); 217 volumes collected; 212 used after discarding first 5
neuroimaging_methods.preprocessing_software_exact: Data Processing Assistant for Resting-State fMRI (DPARSF), based on Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM8)
neuroimaging_methods.normalization_template_exact: Montreal Neurological Institute template (resampling voxel size = 3 × 3 × 3 mm3)
neuroimaging_methods.smoothing_exact: isotropic Gaussian kernel [full width at half maximum (FWHM) = 6 mm]
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: Image volumes with framewise displacement (FD) > 0.2 mm were scrubbed to reduce the effect of head motion using spline interpolation
neuroimaging_methods.filtering_exact: detrended and filtered (0.01~0.08 Hz); high-pass filtered ROI signals with cut-off frequency 1/w prior to calculation of connectivity matrices; low-pass filtered the correlation coefficient time series with cut-off frequency 1/w
neuroimaging_methods.global_signal_regression_exact: Nuisance covariates were regressed [including Friston 24 head motion parameters and white matter and cerebrospinal fluid signals]
primary_neuroimaging_metrics: SFC (static functional connectivity) - Pearson's correlation, Fisher z-transformed
DFC-Str (dynamic functional connectivity strength) - average of DFC
ALFF-FC (amplitude of low frequency fluctuation of functional connectivity)
statistical_thresholds_exact: FDR correction for connection metrics (SFC, DFC-Str, DFC-SD, ALFF-FC)
General linear model (GLM) with age, sex, and mean FD as covariates
Clustering analyses: uncorrected p < 0.05 for TP comparisons
Pearson's or Spearman's correlation for correlation analyses (uncorrected)
neuroimaging_methods.multiple_comparison_correction_exact: FDR (false discovery rate) for SFC, DFC-Str, DFC-SD, ALFF-FC; no correction stated for TP and correlation analyses
neuroimaging_methods.source_location: Pages 3-4, Data Acquirement, Data Preprocessing, Regions of Interest Selection, Dynamic Functional Connectivity Network Analysis, Clustering Analysis, Statistical Analysis sections

extraction_notes.note: No sham acupuncture arm or control intervention condition was included. The study lacks a sham/placebo control for the acupuncture treatment phase. Authors acknowledge this as a limitation.
No expectancy, credibility, blinding success, or allocation guessing measures were assessed or reported in this study.
extraction_notes.source_location: Full paper; no mention in methods or results

extraction_notes.note: Adverse events are not reported. The paper does not include a dedicated adverse events section.

The coordinate space (MNI or Talairach) for neuroimaging results is not explicitly stated in the paper. The normalization template used was MNI, suggesting results are likely in MNI space, but this is not confirmed explicitly for reported connectivity results.

No peak MNI coordinates are reported for the significant DFC or SFC findings. Results are described as connectivity pairs (ROI to ROI using AAL template) without spatial coordinates for individual voxel peaks.

Sample sizes are inconsistent across analyses. For MRI: 17 tinnitus patients pre-acupuncture; 12 post-acupuncture. For clinical scales: 14 patients post-acupuncture. For hearing levels: 15 pre (11 with MRI), 11 post (10 with MRI). These different n values reflect missing data patterns not fully explained.

The paper describes the SFC result as 'SFC between the left posterior cingulate cortex (PCC) and right angular gyrus (ANG)' in the text but Figure 1 caption labels them as 'PCG.L' (posterior cingulate gyrus, left) and 'ANG.R' (angular gyrus, right). There may be a minor discrepancy between text and figure labeling (PCC vs PCG).
extraction_notes.source_location: Page 5, Static Functional Connectivity section; Figure 1 caption

extraction_notes.note: The DFC-Str result (pre vs post) references 'left PCC and right ANG' in the text results section, but the figure caption for Figure 4 uses 'PCG.L' and 'ANG.R'. The paper uses PCC and PCG interchangeably to refer to the same region.
extraction_notes.source_location: Page 6, Dynamic Functional Connectivity section; Figure 4 caption

extraction_notes.note: The correlation of decreased DFC-Str between PCC and ANG with TDI scores references 'left PCC and left ANG' in the results section text, but elsewhere the significant DFC pair is described as 'left PCC and right ANG.' This may be a typographical inconsistency in the paper.
extraction_notes.source_location: Page 6, Dynamic Functional Connectivity section, paragraph starting 'To further explore the relationship'

extraction_notes.note: Formal deqi sensation measures (e.g., MASS scale or Southampton Needle Sensation Questionnaire) were not used. Deqi is described qualitatively only.
Additional acupoints beyond the 7 obligatory ones were selected according to meridian diagnosis and patient symptoms, but these additional acupoints are not individually listed in the paper.

The clustering analysis used k-means with L1 (Manhattan) distance, 4 clusters determined by elbow criterion. The states are labeled by the paper as 'hyper-connected' (state 3) and 'hypo-connected' (state 1) based on visual inspection of cluster centroids shown in Figures 5A and 7A. These labels are the paper's own characterization.
extraction_notes.source_location: Pages 6, 9, Clustering and State Analysis section; Figures 5A, 7A

extraction_notes.note: The paper does not report the n for the between-group DFC analyses (tinnitus vs control). Presumably 17 tinnitus patients and 22 controls, but this is not stated explicitly for individual DFC analyses.
The study is not formally registered as a clinical trial. No trial registration number is provided.

The paper states FDR correction was applied for SFC, DFC-Str, DFC-SD, and ALFF-FC connection metrics, but the TP (transition probability) comparisons from clustering analysis were reported as uncorrected. The correlation analyses were also reported as uncorrected. The FDR threshold level (e.g., q < 0.05) is not explicitly stated.
